subject: Partner integration pact: compatibility safeguards & test matrix
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@nimblestack.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partner request — stability guarantees and lightweight callback header

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — NimbleStack is excited about tightening our embedding + retrieval integration with Redwood. As we scope a tighter production integration (pilot Q3), two items have come up from our engineering and compliance teams and they need to be explicitly addressed before we commit to an expanded pilot: 

1) Minor-version contract stability: We asked Engineering to rely on a minor semantic version bump (e.g., 1.7 -> 1.8) not introducing breaking field removals without 6 months notice. Can Redwood publish a partner-facing compatibility pact that restricts non-breaking guarantees for minor bumps, or provide a partner opt-in that preserves prior fields and behaviors for a defined runway?

2) Optional callback header for request tracing: Our platform uses an internal X-Nimble-Trace header for cross-service tracing and we need a supported, low-overhead header that Redwood will continue to accept even when evolving request shapes. Ideally a documented header space (X-Partner-Trace or similar) and an implementation that ignores unknown subfields but preserves them in logs for audit.

We captured the ask in a short matrix and attached it (nimble_compat_matrix_filled.xlsx). Can the team review and propose a minimal path forward? We don’t need a full policy right away — a one-off partner agreement that we can iterate into a productized compatibility manifest would be sufficient.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Director, Platform Integrations
NimbleStack
(attachment: nimble_compat_matrix_filled.xlsx)

Subject: Re: Partner request — stability guarantees and lightweight callback header

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the matrix, this is helpful. We're sympathetic to predictable upgrades for partners and the tracing/header space request is reasonable. Next steps from our side: 

- I've attached a proposed compatibility matrix template that outlines the minimum guarantees we can commit to for partner pilots (redwood-proposed-compat-matrix.xlsx).
- We will review your filled matrix and give a line-by-line response.
- Suggest a short technical working session (30–45m) next week to align on the header semantics and a test harness for the compatibility checks.

Can you do Tue 8 May or Thu 10 May PST? Ben — can you validate whether a 6-month runway for minor bumps is operationally feasible with current runtime constraints? Vanessa — can you confirm whether Partnerships will accept a temporary bilateral doc (partner compatibility pact) that later converts into a published policy?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Marissa — Tue 8 May PST works for us (10:00am PT preferred). Thanks for the template — we completed one column to show priority. Two clarifications from our engineers: 

- We don't require a global product-level toggle initially; a partner-specific opt-in + response headers describing compatibility mode are fine.
- For the header, we propose "X-Partner-Context" with a simple JSON payload (key-value). We understand Redwood will not parse arbitrary content but needs to store/forward the header for observability.

I've re-attached the matrix we filled (nimble_compat_matrix_filled.xlsx) and labeled high-priority rows. Looking forward to the working session.

Subject: Re: Partner request — stability guarantees and lightweight callback header

Marissa / team / Alex — I dug into runtime and release cadence constraints. Quick summary and two proposed options: 

Option A (preferred, low lift):
- Partner-specific compatibility flag on our routing layer that preserves deprecated fields for flagged partners for 180 days after a minor bump.
- Partners sign a short paper (Partner Compatibility Addendum) that lists feature rows from the matrix.
- Redwood publishes a machine-readable compatibility response header when a compatibility flag is active (e.g., X-Redwood-Compat: partner=nimblestack;expires=2028-11-01).

Option B (stricter, productized):
- Formalize a published compatibility manifest in Console; requires product timeline (Q4) and SDK work to honor the manifest across clients.

Constraints / notes:
- We cannot promise zero-risk for field additions that change semantics (we can promise presence and preserved serialization for 180 days).
- Runtime changes that affect kernel selection or quantization paths are out of scope for compatibility flags.

If NimbleStack is OK with Option A, we can fast-track a Partner Compatibility Addendum and enable routing-layer flags for the pilot. Proposed working-session agenda attached in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2B3C-redwood-proposed-compat-matrix

Next actions: Marissa to confirm partnership/legal sign-off approach; Vanessa to confirm the bilateral doc path and whether Partnerships can be listed as the owning org. Alex — can you confirm that the 180-day runway meets NimbleStack's operational requirements?

Ben Carter
Director, Product @ Redwood Inference
